title: Phase I study on immunochemotherapy combined with hyperthermia as first line therapy in patients with locally advanced and metastatic biliary tract cancer
summary:
Biliary tract tumours are rare, aggressive cancers with an often poor prognosis. The current standard treatment for advanced disease is combined immunochemotherapy, but its effectiveness is limited (median overall survival approx. 12 months). Hyperthermia (= targeted heating of the tumour to 40–43 °C) activates the immune system, which could enhance the effect of immunochemotherapy. The aim of the planned study is to investigate whether the combination of immunochemotherapy and hyperthermia can improve the response to therapy and thus positively influence tumour regression, prevent relapse and improve survival rates. 

As part of the study, all patients will receive standard therapy with gemcitabine, cisplatin and durvalumab or pembrolizumab every 3 weeks. In addition, a 90-minute hyperthermia treatment will be given on the day before the infusion. This is generally considered to be very low in side effects, so we do not expect any additional stress for the participants. There may be a feeling of warmth, sweating or, very rarely, slight pain and skin redness.

In addition, we plan to use blood and tissue samples to analyse markers for response at the cellular level in order to gain a deeper understanding of the biological effects.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of other and unspecified parts of biliary tract

interventions.name: Additional regional hyperthermia (RHT) to the current standard immune chemotherapy (Gem + Cis + Durva/Pembro). RHT is applied twice per cycle and 24 hours prior to the administration of the standard ICT until progression.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1)	Signed informed consent form, including the translational study program
2)	Age ≥18 years
3)	ECOG 0–1
4)	Histologically confirmed biliary tract carcinoma (intra-/extrahepatic cholangiocellular carcinoma, gallbladder carcinoma)
5)	Locally advanced and unresectable disease, metastatic disease
6)	Previously untreated disease
7)	No prior chemotherapy or checkpoint inhibitor therapy
8)	Recurrence >6 months after initial curative resection
9)	At least 1 target lesion according to iRECIST and RECIST 1.1
10)	Adequate organ and bone marrow function
a.	Haemoglobin ≥9.0 g/dL
b.	ANC ≥1.5 × 10⁹/L
c.	Platelets ≥100 × 10⁹/L
d.	Serum bilirubin ≤2.5 × upper limit of normal (ULN) (higher values permitted for confirmed Meulengracht’s disease based on individual assessment)
e.	Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) + aspartate aminotransferase (AST) ≤2.5 × ULN. 
f.	Creatinine clearance >50 mL/min 
11)	Life expectancy ≥3 months
12)	Willingness to provide biological material
Exclusion criteria:
1)	Metal implants or dense clusters of metal clips in the hyperthermia treatment area
2)	Active or previous autoimmune disease, except for the following:
a.	Vitiligo
b.	Hashimoto’s thyroiditis
c.	Chronic skin disease not requiring systemic treatment
d.	Patients without active disease in the past 5 years may be included after consultation with the study physician.
e.	Patients with celiac disease managed solely through dietary control
3)	Known allergy to any of the study medications
4)	Any contraindication to regional hyperthermia or a condition that makes hyperthermia impossible (e.g., seroma, metal implants in the hyperthermia area, severe obesity)
5)	History of allogeneic organ transplantation
6)	History of other malignant diseases, except for
a.	Cancer that has been curatively treated and has been in remission for <5 years with a low risk of recurrence
b.	Adequately treated non-melanoma skin cancer or lentigo maligna in remission
c.	Adequately treated carcinoma in situ in remission
7)	History of leptomeningeal carcinomatosis
8)	History of active primary immunodeficiency
9)	Acute infection (including tuberculosis, hepatitis B/C, HIV)
10)	Any unresolved toxicity ≥ CTCAE Grade 2 from prior cancer treatment
11)	Brain metastases (patients with suspected brain metastases should undergo an MRI scan of the brain, preferably with intravenous contrast, prior to study enrolment)
12)	Spinal cord compression
13)	Pregnant women
